'''Moungi Gabriel Bawendi'''<ref name="AnalysisAndGeom"/> (born 15 March 1961)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tunisienumerique.com/le-tunisien-moungi-g-bawendi-parmi-les-laureats-du-prix-nobel-de-chimie/|title=Le Tunisien Moungi G. Bawendi parmi les lauréats du prix Nobel de chimie|first=Mohsen|last=Tiss|date=October 4, 2023|website=Tunisie}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://kapitalis.com/tunisie/2023/10/04/le-tunisien-moungi-bawendi-parmi-le-trois-prix-nobel-de-chimie-2023/|title=Le Tunisien Moungi Bawendi parmi le trois Prix Nobel de chimie 2023|date=October 4, 2023}}</ref> is an American [[chemist]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last1=Devlin |first1=Hannah |date=2023-10-04 |title=Scientists share Nobel prize in chemistry for quantum dots discovery |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2023/oct/04/nobel-prize-in-chemistry-winners-2023 |access-date=2023-10-04 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jmaterenvironsci.com/Document/vol7/vol7_N4/121-JMES-2150-Turki.pdf |title=An overview of the main Tunisian scientists in Chemistry and Materials Science |accessdate=October 5, 2020}}</ref> He is currently the [[Lester Wolfe]] Professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://chemistry.mit.edu/people/bawendi-moungi|title=Moungi Bawendi|publisher=mit.edu|accessdate=May 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821233045/http://chemistry.mit.edu/people/bawendi-moungi|archive-date=August 21, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://nanocluster.mit.edu/|title=Moungi Bawendi|publisher=mit.edu|accessdate=May 1, 2017}}</ref> Bawendi is known for his advances in the chemical production of high-quality [[quantum dot]]s.<ref name="NobelPrize">{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2023 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2023/press-release/ |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> For this work, he was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] in 2023.

== Early life ==
Moungi Bawendi was born in [[Paris]], France, the son of Tunisian mathematician [[M. Salah Baouendi|Mohammed Salah Baouendi]]. After periods living in France and [[Tunisia]], Bawendi and his family migrated to the United States when he was a child.<ref name="AnalysisAndGeom">{{Cite book |last1=Baklouti |first1=Ali |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4NVECgAAQBAJ&dq=moungi+bawendi+Fran%C3%A7ais&pg=PA4 |title=Analysis and Geometry: MIMS-GGTM, Tunis, Tunisia, 2014. In Honour of Mohammed Salah Baouendi|last2=El Kacimi |first2=Aziz |last3=Kallel |first3=Sadok |last4=Mir |first4=Nordine |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |year=2015 |isbn=9783319174426 |location=Heidelberg |language=en |access-date=4 October 2023}}</ref> They lived in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]], as Salah worked in the math department at [[Purdue University]].<ref name="AnalysisAndGeom"/> Bawendi graduated from [[West Lafayette Junior-Senior High School]] in 1978.<ref name="WallOfPride2022">{{cite web |title=Distinguished West Lafayette Alumni to Return for Wall of Pride Celebration |url=https://wlsef.org/event/distinguished-west-lafayette-alumni-to-return-for-wall-of-pride-celebration/ |website=West Lafayette Schools Education Foundation |access-date=4 October 2023}}</ref><ref name="BasedInLaf2023">{{cite news |last1=Bangert |first1=Dave |title=West Lafayette grad awarded Nobel Prize in Chemistry |url=https://www.basedinlafayette.com/p/west-lafayette-grad-awarded-nobel |access-date=5 October 2023 |work=www.basedinlafayette.com |date=4 October 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Higher education and career ===
Bawendi received both an [[Bachelor of Arts|A.B.]] in 1982<ref>{{cite news |title=University of Chicago alum shares Nobel Prize in Chemistry - CBS Chicago |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/university-of-chicago-alum-nobel-prize-chemistry/ |work=CBS News |date=4 October 2023}}</ref>  and an [[Master of Arts|A.M.]] in 1983 from [[Harvard University]].<ref name="Gregersen">{{cite web |last1=Gregersen |first1=Erik |title=Moungi Bawendi {{!}} Biography, Nobel Prize, Quantum Dots, & Facts {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Moungi-Bawendi |website=www.britannica.com|date=October 6, 2023 |language=en |access-date=6 October 2023}}</ref> He earned a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in chemistry in 1988 from the [[University of Chicago]],<ref name="NobelPrize" /> under the supervision of [[Karl Freed]] and [[Takeshi Oka]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Bawendi |first=Moungi Gabriel |url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/273239dfdb1eef49fa8a705d290a3d76/1?pq-origsite=gscholar&cbl=18750&diss=y |title=From the Biggest to the Smallest Polyatomic Molecules: Statistical Mechanics and Quantum Mechanics in Action |publisher=University of Chicago |year=1988 |type=PhD Dissertation}}</ref>

With Freed, Bawendi worked on theoretical [[polymer physics]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2023-10-04 |title=UChicago alum Moungi Bawendi shares Nobel Prize in Chemistry for discovery of quantum dots {{!}} University of Chicago News |url=https://news.uchicago.edu/story/uchicago-alum-moungi-bawendi-shares-nobel-prize-chemistry-discovery-quantum-dots |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=news.uchicago.edu |language=en}}</ref>  and with Oka, Bawendi worked on experiments on hot-bands of [[trihydrogen cation|H<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>]], which played a role in deciphering the emission spectrum of [[Jupiter (planet)|Jupiter]] observed in 1989.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Oka |first=Takeshi |date=2013-10-03 |title=My 45 Years of Astrochemistry: Memoirs of Takeshi Oka |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A |language=en |volume=117 |issue=39 |pages=9308–9313 |doi=10.1021/jp4035826 |pmid=24490724 |bibcode=2013JPCA..117.9308O |issn=1089-5639|doi-access=free }}</ref>

During his graduate studies, Oka recommended Bawendi to a summer program in [[Bell Labs]], where [[Louis E. Brus]] introduced Bawendi to the research on quantum dots.<ref name=":1" /> Upon graduation, Bawendi went to work with Brus at Bell Labs as a [[postdoctoral researcher]].<ref name=":2" />

Bawendi joined [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1990 and became professor in 1996.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=2023-10-04 |title=Names of purported Nobel chemistry prize winners inadvertently released |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/names-purported-nobel-chemistry-prize-winners-inadvertently-released-2023-10-04/ |access-date=2023-10-04}}</ref>

==Research==
Bawendi was one of the most cited [[chemist]]s of the decade from 2000 to 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most cited chemists |url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100Chemists2000-10/ |accessdate=July 28, 2017 |publisher=Thomson Reuters}}</ref> He is a leading figure in the research and development of [[quantum dot]]s.<ref name="NobelPrize" /> Quantum dots are tiny [[Semiconductor|semiconducting]] [[crystal]]s whose nanoscale size gives them unique optical and [[Electronic configuration|electronic properties]].<ref name="Singh">{{cite journal |last1=Singh |first1=Suchita |last2=Dhawan |first2=Aksha |last3=Karhana |first3=Sonali |last4=Bhat |first4=Madhusudan |last5=Dinda |first5=Amit Kumar |title=Quantum Dots: An Emerging Tool for Point-of-Care Testing |journal=Micromachines |date=29 November 2020 |volume=11 |issue=12 |pages=1058 |doi=10.3390/mi11121058 |pmid=33260478 |pmc=7761335 |issn=2072-666X |doi-access=free }}</ref>

A major challenge in quantum dot research was to find ways to create high quality quantum dots that are stable and uniform.  Bawendi is recognized for his work in developing standardized methods for quantum dot synthesis. In 1993, Bawendi, and his PhD students David J. Norris and [[Christopher B. Murray]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Robinson |first=Julia |title=The quantum dot story |url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/features/the-quantum-dot-story/4018219.article |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Chemistry World |language=en}}</ref> reported on a hot-injection synthesis method for producing reproducible quantum dots with well-defined size and with high optical quality. 
This breakthrough in chemical production methods made it possible to “tune” quantum dots according to size, and achieve predictable properties as a result.  It gave scientists much greater control over the material, and made it possible to achieve precise and reproducible results.<ref name="Palma"/><ref name="Heiner"/>

The method opened the door to the development of large-scale technological applications of quantum dots in a wide range of areas.<ref name="Palma">{{cite news |last1=Palma |first1=Jasmine |last2=Wang |first2=Austin H. |title=One Small Quantum Dot, One Giant Leap for Nanoscience: Moungi Bawendi '82 Wins Nobel Prize in Chemistry {{!}} News {{!}} The Harvard Crimson |url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2023/10/6/nanoscience-bawendi-chemistry-nobel/ |work=The Harvard Crimson |date=October 6, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Heiner">{{Cite journal |last=Linke |first=Heiner |date=3 October 2023 |title=Quantum dots — seeds of nanoscience |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2023/10/advanced-chemistryprize2023.pdf |journal=The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences}}</ref> Quantum dots are now used in [[light-emitting diode]]s (LEDs), [[photovoltaics]] (solar cells),<ref name="Cotta"/> [[photodetector]]s, [[photoconductors]], lasers,<ref name="Lerner">{{cite news |last1=Lerner |first1=Eric J. |title=Introduction to photodetectors and applications |url=https://www.laserfocusworld.com/detectors-imaging/article/16555513/introduction-to-photodetectors-and-applications |work=Laser Focus World |date=1 December 2000}}</ref> [[biomedical imaging]], [[biosensing]] and other applications.<ref name="Cotta">{{cite journal |last1=Cotta |first1=Mônica A. |title=Quantum Dots and Their Applications: What Lies Ahead? |journal=[[ACS Applied Nano Materials]] |date=26 June 2020 |volume=3 |issue=6 |pages=4920–4924 |doi=10.1021/acsanm.0c01386 |bibcode=2020ACSAN...3.4920C |s2cid=225779939 |language=en |issn=2574-0970|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

Bawendi was granted the [[Sloan Research Fellowship]] in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Database |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=Alfred P Sloan Foundation}}</ref> He won the 1997 Nobel Signature Award for Graduate Education in Chemistry of [[American Chemical Society]] (ACS).<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=American Chemical Society's president comments on award of 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry |url=https://www.acs.org/pressroom/newsreleases/2023/october/acs-president-comments-on-award-of-2023-nobel-prize-in-chemistry.html |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref> In 2001, he received the [[Sackler Prize]] in Physical Chemistry of Advanced Materials.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-09-05 |title=Past Laureates of the Raymond and Beverly Sackler International Prize in the Physical Sciences |url=https://english.tau.ac.il/sackler_prize_in_chemistry_past_laureates |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=Tel Aviv University |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2006, he was awarded the [[Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-16 |title=LAWRENCE Award Laureates {{!}} U.S. DOE Office of Science (SC) |url=https://science.osti.gov/lawrence/Award-Laureates |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=science.osti.gov |language=en-US}}</ref>

He was elected member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2003,<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 31, 2003 |title=AAAS Elects Fellows in Chemistry |url=http://pubsapp.acs.org/cen/awards/8113/8113awards1.html? |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=Chemical and Engineering News |type=volume 81}}</ref> of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2004,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Member Directory {{!}} American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/directory |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=www.amacad.org}}</ref> and of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2007.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Moungi G. Bawendi |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/moungi-gabriel-bawendi-yvrroj/ |access-date=2023-10-05 |website=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

In 2010 during the National Meeting on March 23, 2010, Bawendi received the [[ACS Awards|ACS Award]] in [[Colloid]] and [[Surface science|Surface Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2010 |title=Dresselhaus and Bawendi Honored by ACS |url=https://web.mit.edu/spectroscopy/events/newsletter/news_v26_n2.pdf |journal=MIT the Spectrograph |volume=26}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> He also received the 2011 [[SEMI]] Award for North America for quantum dot research.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2012 |title=QD Vision receives the SEMI Award for quantum dot research |url=https://www.semi.org/en/qd-vision-receives-semi-award-quantum-dot-research}}</ref>

Bawendi was selected as a [[List of Clarivate Citation laureates in Chemistry|Clarivate Citation Laureate in Chemistry]] in 2020, jointly with [[Christopher B. Murray]] and [[Hyeon Taeghwan]], "for synthesis of [[Nanocrystallites|nanocrystals]] with precise attributes for a wide range of applications in physical, biological, and medical systems.".<ref>{{Cite press release |last=Plc |first=Clarivate |title=Clarivate Reveals 2020 Citation Laureates - Annual List of Researchers of Nobel Class |url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/clarivate-reveals-2020-citation-laureates---annual-list-of-researchers-of-nobel-class-301136248.html |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=www.prnewswire.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Bawendi was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry]] jointly with [[Louis E. Brus]] and [[Alexey Ekimov]] "for the discovery and synthesis of [[quantum dot]]s".<ref name=":0" />

He was elected to the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 2026.<ref>{{cite news |title=MIT community members elected to the National Academy of Engineering for 2026 |url=https://news.mit.edu/2026/mit-community-members-elected-national-academy-engineering-0217 |access-date=19 February 2026 |work=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |date=17 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> He was also awarded the Medal of Honor by [[Tunis University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leaders.com.tn/article/35908-bawendi-a-l-enit-sur-les-traces-de-son-pere-le-prix-nobel-chimie-en-consecration-album-photos|title=Bawendi à l'ENIT… sur les traces de son père, le Prix Nobel Chimie en consécration|date=2011-01-22 |access-date=2024-05-22}}</ref> In 2025, he received a [[Carnegie Corporation of New York]] [[Great Immigrants Award|Great Immigrant Award]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-26 |title=Carnegie honors 20 'Great Immigrants,' including composer Tania León, for 20th anniversary |url=https://apnews.com/article/carnegie-corp-great-immigrants-great-americans-tania-leon-fde162cd204af3d998575a6fa39fccea |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=AP News |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bawendi is married to [[journalist]] Rachel Zimmerman, widow of a computer science MIT professor, [[Seth J. Teller]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Zimmerman |first=Rachel |date=October 14, 2023 |title=Our lives had been shattered. Now something extraordinary was happening. |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wellness/2023/10/14/grief-healing-families-joy}}</ref>
